source.title: Towards Understanding and Improving Refusal in Compressed Models via Mechanistic Interpretability

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some tables and figure values appear flattened or are available only as plots.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses difference-in-means refusal directions and applies directional ablation and activation addition, following the original method, on compressed models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ablation and activation-addition outcomes in figures, but does not give exact plotted scores in the text. Table 3 gives selected direction positions, which are selection results rather than intervention outcomes. AIRD results are omitted from the rows because AIRD is the paper's own weight-edit method and its reported safety and capability outcomes do not test the claim's specified removal or addition. Table 5 compares independently extracted directions; those cosine similarities do not establish behavioral transfer.
record.test_reason: It applies Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means extraction, directional ablation and activation addition unchanged to a new setting: pruned and quantized Llama2-7b-chat and Llama3-8b-instruct. It reports refusal outcomes of both interventions per compressed model (Figs 3–6). The method matches the original (T1-like), but the contribution is the compressed-model setting, so T3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude refusal in compressed models is still mediated by a single direction, validated by ablation (necessity) and ActAdd (sufficiency). Pruning shifts the direction's source and lowers its similarity to the original, while quantization preserves it, which they offer as the mechanistic reason quantized models are safer. The safety link is correlational. AIRD raises safety in pruned models without significant benchmark loss and leaves the direction unchanged (cos ≈0.99).
record.recipe_differences: The paper follows the original difference-in-means, directional-ablation, and activation-addition approach, applying it to compressed Llama models. It also selects directions using its described validation procedure and focuses on compression conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression method and, for Wanda pruning, calibration dataset affect the selected direction's source position; cosine similarities to the original directions also differ by compression method.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity between directions extracted from compressed and original models is about 0.99 under quantization but 0.34–0.54 for pruned Llama2 and 0.73–0.90 for pruned Llama3. Selected layer or position shifts only under pruning. Authors correlate this with higher post-compression ASR (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning, but not post-training quantization, relocates and rotates the refusal direction, which co-occurs with safety loss.

fits_no_version.finding: AIRD writes the original uncompressed model's direction into the pruned model's output projections with small α. This lowers ASR by up to 41% relative (Table 6), with benchmark changes within ±2 points (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The uncompressed model's refusal direction can partially restore refusal when injected into its pruned variant (possible weak V6 evidence, via the authors' own method).

record.problems: The main ablation and addition outcomes are presented in figures without exact scores in the text. Refusal is measured by substring matching. The paper does not report uncertainty for these intervention results, and its general-capability evaluation is for AIRD rather than directional ablation.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 direction positions were omitted because they are used to identify/select directions, not reported intervention outcomes. Table 4 compression ASR results were omitted because they compare compression safety without intervening on the refusal direction. AIRD safety results in Table 6 and AIRD capability results in Table 7 were omitted because they evaluate the paper's own weight-edit method rather than the claim's specified ablation or activation addition. Table 10 AIRD direction similarities were also omitted because they are results for that new method.

untested.parts: Preservation of other abilities under directional ablation. Capability benchmarks cover only AIRD; ablation is constrained only by the selection kl_score<0.1. The exact post-intervention refusal and ASR magnitudes are plot-only.
No abliteration weight edit that removes refusal.
Jailbreaks are evaluated but not linked to direction suppression; no adversarial training against ablation.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction accounts. The single-direction finding is asserted, not compared against alternatives.
No behavioural test of a direction carried across model variants, languages or base→instruct. Only cosine similarity of separately extracted directions is reported.
Not addressed; compression calibration data is varied, not refusal training.

missing.what: No-intervention baseline bar labels are readable (ASR ~0.01–0.05 on harmful; refusal 0.01 on harmless) but rows record 'figure only'.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'challenges' label is dropped: the study never tests multi-direction or affine accounts, so V4 is untested. 'Partial' states were unsupported because no incompleteness is shown; the authors' words and captions indicate the effect occurred, though exact intervention magnitudes are plot-only. Llama3 magnitude pruning was excluded due to performance collapse. The text mislabels the sufficiency test prompts as harmful; the figures show harmless prompts. Refusal is scored by substring matching, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The text reports significant changes in refusal-related scores, but does not establish that ablation removes nearly all refusals or that ablation preserves general capabilities. The reported general benchmarks evaluate AIRD, not the ablation.
The paper does not test a weight edit that removes refusal.
The paper evaluates adversarial attacks but does not test whether they suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The paper tests its single-direction account in compressed models, not whether refusal is affine or cone-shaped in other settings.
The paper does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.

The paper compares independently extracted directions across compressed and uncompressed models, but does not test whether one direction transferred from one model carries refusal behavior in another. It does not test language transfer or base-to-instruct transfer.
The paper varies compression calibration data, not how or when refusal training creates the direction.

relationships.condition: Llama2-7b-chat (Wanda-Align, Wanda-Alpaca, Magnitude, LLM.int8, AWQ) and Llama3-8b-instruct (Wanda-Align, Wanda-Alpaca, LLM.int8, AWQ), 50% sparsity or 8-bit
relationships.reason: Ablating each compressed model's own diff-in-means direction raises ASR from ~0.01–0.05 baselines (r1–r5, r11–r14). Adding it raises harmless refusal from 0.01 (r6–r10, r15–r18). Magnitudes are plot-only.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating each compressed model’s own direction increased attack success from approximately 0.01–0.05 baselines, while addition increased harmless refusal from 0.01.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested compressed Llama2-7b and Llama3-8b configurations
reader_labels.reason: Ablation and addition move the reported refusal-related scores in the expected directions, but the text only reports significant increases and does not show refusal being fully removed or uniformly induced (r1-r18).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Tested compressed Llama2-7b and Llama3-8b configurations
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that interventions on the extracted single direction change refusal-related outcomes, consistent with a single-direction account in these tested models, though the plotted effect sizes are not stated in the text (r1-r18).
